claims.claim_text: On the audited next-prime filter (`prime_gap` trace id), the certified learned rule gate improves top-1 over both the raw scorer and the hand-wheel gate while preserving zero false rejections.
claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The audited next-prime learned-gate delta is not currently supported by the canonical comparison rows, so the 9.13% -> 45.12% -> 68.87% progression cannot be used as a headline claim.
claims.summary: the verified learned filter raises top-1 ranking to 68.87% from 45.12% for the hand-coded wheel and 9.13% raw, with 0 verifier-counted true-answer deletions.
claims.title: Audited next-prime filter improves top-1 over raw and hand-wheel gates

claims.claim_text: On the audited next-prime filter (`prime_gap` trace id), the certified learned rule gate improves top-1 over raw and hand-wheel gates across a multi-seed audit while preserving zero false rejections.
claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The audited next-prime learned-gate headline lacks a supported multi-seed interval, so the 9.13% -> 45.12% -> 68.87% progression should be treated as a single artifact snapshot.
claims.summary: across 5 seeds, the learned filter stays at 68.87% +/- 0.00pp, versus 45.12% +/- 0.00pp for the hand wheel and 9.13% +/- 0.00pp raw; the worst learned-vs-hand gain is +23.74pp, learned top-10 never falls below 100.00%, and false rejections never exceed 0; promotion requires 5 seeds.
claims.title: Audited next-prime filter headline is stable across seeds

claims.claim_text: On the audited next-prime filter (`prime_gap` trace id), the neural rule proposer is useful at fixed verifier budget relative to grammar-order and structural baselines.

contradicted_if: neural_structural trails grammar_order and structural_heuristic on any reported grammar

claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The current fixed-budget next-prime proposer evidence is negative for static neural proposer superiority; Axis 2 remains a falsifiable baseline failure until R-E2.1/R-E2.2/R-E2.3 close the gap.
residual: Treat the current Axis 2 row as a negative or mixed result, not a proposer-usefulness proof.
Run R-E2.1 for 5+ seeds and budget grids.
Run R-E2.2/R-E2.3 only if the richer grammar creates non-saturated cases where learned ordering can matter.
claims.summary: the static neural proposer loses to deterministic ordering in at least one grammar: candidate static saves 72.49 vs grammar 73.22, and conditional static saves 2.15 vs grammar 55.57.
claims.title: Next-prime neural proposer beats fixed-budget symbolic baselines

claims.claim_text: When trained on the fixed ARC task but evaluated on held-out same-envelope ARC variants, the shared multitask scorer beats the single-task ARC scorer.
claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The ARC same-envelope OOD transfer claim is not supported, so shared scoring should be treated as a substrate ablation rather than a positive transfer result.
claims.paper_explanation: This supports the narrow residual-generalization claim: the shared scorer loses on the fixed ARC training task, but improves held-out same-envelope ARC ranking and log loss.
claims.summary: shared OOD top-1 48.40% vs single 42.83% (+5.57pp), NLL 2.6278 vs 4.3723.
claims.title: Shared scorer beats single-task scorer on same-envelope ARC OOD

claims.claim_text: The public ARC certified transform gate and budgeted proposer measurements are unchanged under shared-scorer and single-task-scorer context labels in the current implementation.
claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The public ARC gate/proposer rows are not invariant to scorer context labels, so they cannot cleanly separate gate correctness from scorer transfer.
claims.paper_explanation: This separates the certified ARC gate from learned scorer choice: the public ARC gate/proposer measurements are currently scorer-independent, so scorer claims and gate claims remain cleanly separated.
claims.summary: ARC gate/proposer invariance holds across scorer-context labels: train 24/400 certified tasks, eval 4/400, mismatches=0.
claims.title: Public ARC certified gate is invariant to scorer context labels

claims.claim_text: The generated evidence reports public ARC train/eval certified-task and covered-cell counts as a measured surface rather than as a broad ARC-performance claim.

supported_if: latest measured evaluation certified_tasks >= v12_recorded evaluation certified_tasks
latest measured evaluation test_correct_cells >= v12_recorded evaluation test_correct_cells

claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The public ARC evidence surface is missing or regressed, so the claim set should not include a committed public-corpus parity row.
claims.paper_explanation: This is not a broad ARC-performance claim. It is the public-corpus parity row: the compiler can now distinguish measured ARC gate coverage, version-to-version movement, and the much larger unresolved residual.
claims.summary: the ARC row measures coverage, not competence: public eval coverage moves from v10 4 tasks/187 cells to v15_measured 7 tasks/1057 cells, while train coverage is 24 tasks/1187 cells.
claims.title: Public ARC corpus parity row is measured and scoped

claims.claim_text: On ARC, the shared scorer improves log loss but worsens fixed-task ECE, while improving both log loss and ECE on same-envelope OOD evaluation.
claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The ARC calibration tradeoff is not supported, so the claim set should avoid saying shared scoring improves calibration and should report only the raw NLL/ECE table.
claims.paper_explanation: The calibration claim is explicitly conditional: shared training is not simply better calibrated everywhere. It is worse on fixed ARC ECE but better on OOD ECE, while improving log loss in both settings.
claims.summary: ARC shared scorer is a calibration tradeoff: fixed-task NLL improves (4.0827 vs 8.2754) while ECE worsens (0.6995 vs 0.5589); OOD improves both NLL (2.6278 vs 4.3723) and ECE (0.4481 vs 0.4820).
claims.title: ARC shared scorer has a fixed-task versus OOD calibration tradeoff

claims.claim_text: Delayed_claim benefits from shared training at matched updates, but the sibling effect is specific rather than universal.
claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The delayed_claim leave-one-out rows do not support positive sibling transfer, so delayed_claim should not be used as a positive multitask example.
claims.paper_explanation: This replaces the earlier broad positive-transfer claim with a narrower one: delayed_claim benefits from shared training in this envelope, grid_path appears to be the helpful sibling, and ARC is mild interference.
claims.summary: delayed_claim all-domain top-1 98.00% vs claim-only 96.60% (+1.40pp); removing grid_path falls to 97.20%, while removing ARC rises to 98.50%.
claims.title: Delayed-claim transfer gain is sibling-specific

claims.claim_text: A four-capacity sweep changes the fixed ARC shared-vs-single gap but does not monotonically close it, while delayed_claim remains non-negative across capacities.

supported_if: all ARC capacity rows have seeds >= 3
ARC delta is not monotone non-decreasing with parameter count

claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The capacity sweep no longer rules out a simple width explanation, so adapters or ordering should not be treated as the next architectural bottleneck without a new plateau audit.
claims.paper_explanation: This keeps the architecture roadmap disciplined: capacity changes the ARC gap, but does not monotonically close it, so adapters or ordering should not be claimed until the tiny-net plateau check is done.
claims.summary: making the shared model wider does not simply fix ARC: the best fixed-ARC shared row is 32x16 at 39.20%, but every shared ARC row trails single-task; delayed_claim deltas remain +0.10pp to +0.43pp.
claims.title: Capacity sweep does not explain away the ARC fixed-task gap

claims.claim_text: A single compact shared trunk with small domain-specific heads is considered the promoted architecture only if it improves fixed ARC versus the flat shared scorer while preserving delayed-claim transfer, grid-path performance, and ARC OOD relative to single-task.

diagnostic_if: task heads help fixed ARC but hurt OOD or delayed-claim transfer
supported_if: shared_task_heads fixed ARC top1 > flat_shared fixed ARC top1
shared_task_heads delayed_claim top1 is no worse than flat_shared by more than 0.5pp
shared_task_heads grid_path top1 is no worse than flat_shared by more than 0.5pp
shared_task_heads ARC OOD top1 >= single_task ARC OOD top1
shared_task_heads ARC OOD NLL <= single_task ARC OOD NLL

claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The shared-trunk/domain-head architecture has not passed all promotion gates, so it should be presented as architecture evidence rather than the default model recipe.
claims.paper_explanation: The adapter-head result is treated as an architecture gate, not a broad one-model claim. A shared trunk plus domain heads is promoted only if it helps fixed ARC without erasing delayed-claim transfer, materially regressing grid_path, or losing same-envelope ARC OOD against the matched single-task baseline.
residual: Keep shared trunk plus domain heads as a diagnostic architecture rather than the default.
Avoid broad all-task competence language; report the fixed ARC, OOD, delayed-claim, grid, and prime rows separately.
Use the flat shared scorer as the interference control until the gates pass.
claims.summary: task-specific heads help some rows and hurt others: fixed ARC heads-flat delta +0.00pp; delayed_claim heads-flat +0.00pp; grid_path heads-flat +0.23pp; ARC OOD heads-single +5.80pp top-1 and -1.2020 NLL.
claims.title: Shared trunk plus domain heads is gated as architecture evidence

claims.claim_text: Verifier rejection reasons can be fed back into the proposer so that reason-aware and trained-residual ranking avoid unsafe rows and improve budgeted validation utility on the arithmetic-sequence/modular gate family.

supported_if: model_score picks unsafe rows and produces validation false rejections at budget 8
reason_prior and trained_residual have zero unsafe rows and zero validation false rejections at budget 8
prime_gap and modular_gate split sweeps have zero trained_residual validation false rejections and nonnegative utility deltas

claims.limitation_when_not_supported: Rejected-candidate reason learning is not yet a supported proposer repair, so Axis 2 should remain only the fixed-budget negative result.
claims.paper_explanation: This is the first feedback loop: rejected verifier rows become reason labels, and those labels improve the next proposal pass. The claim is scoped to the arithmetic-sequence/modular sweeps; delayed_claim remains a stress case. Seed-interval and reason-family artifacts are reported when present so the reporting can distinguish stable proposer repair from a single favorable trace.
claims.summary: logging why the verifier rejected a guess repairs the next-prime proposer at budget 8: the unguided model chooses 7 unsafe rows and causes 172 validation false rejections, while the reason prior reaches 6 accepted rules/216.0 utility and the trained repair reaches 7 accepted rules/245.0 utility with zero false rejections; arithmetic-sequence/modular split sweeps pass, but the delayed-claim stress case has 0 mixed split rows.
claims.title: Rejected-candidate reasons repair proposer ranking on arithmetic/modular gates

claims.claim_text: Zero-false-rejection hypothesis promotions can be reused as slot priors that improve learned proposal coverage and utility in the ARC hypothesis fixture.

supported_if: at least one promoted library row has support_tasks >= 2 and false_rejections == 0
slot_prior learned certified@1 > no_prior learned certified@1
slot_prior learned utility@8 > no_prior learned utility@8
both compared learned rows preserve zero false rejections

claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The certified hypothesis library does not yet produce a supported feedback gain, so it should remain substrate machinery only.
claims.paper_explanation: This makes the hypothesis library a generated claim rather than a roadmap note. Fixture feedback and held-out feedback are separated in machine-readable rows; public ARC promotion remains the R-S.1c gap before using it as a headline ARC claim.
claims.summary: saving repeatedly safe rules helps future tasks: promoted move_to_anchor from 2 tasks/78 covered events with zero false rejections; slot priors raise first-choice certifications from 2 to 4 and budget-8 utility from 0.2119 to 0.5169. Held-out split feedback rows: 30.
claims.title: Certified hypothesis libraries feed back into proposal ranking

claims.claim_text: Before increasing neural capacity, the generated evidence reports a same-ladder tiny-net audit with learning curves, restart variance, best checkpoint, plateau detection, parameter count, FLOPs, and width-help verdicts for each core task.

supported_if: all core domains have the same four-capacity ladder for shared, shared_task_heads, and single_task

claims.claim_text: On held-out replay-certified Signal flight groups, a tiny WASD ranker improves top-1, utility, and regret against the primitive no-safety goal-heading baseline without increasing measured damage or death rate.

supported_if: neural regret is lower than baseline_regret
neural damage and death rates are no worse than baseline on the held-out trace
closed-loop rollout evidence is reported separately as a bridge metric, not as an active multiplayer performance claim

claims.limitation_when_not_supported: Signal does not yet provide a supported replay-control vignette, so Signal should be removed from the abstract and kept only in the roadmap.
claims.paper_explanation: This is an application vignette, not a live-control claim: Signal contributes a replay-certified bounded-control surface where the neural component ranks nine WASD candidates and simulator replay owns the outcome labels. The rollout summary is a closed-loop bridge around certified control-target hypotheses, not a multiplayer performance claim.
claims.summary: in offline Signal replay, the model ranks recorded WASD choices at top-1 79.76% vs baseline 67.86% (+11.90pp), utility 0.1432 vs 0.1359, regret 0.0073 vs 0.0146, damage 2.38% vs 2.38%, deaths 0.00% vs 0.00%; live shadow frames=74. Closed-loop rollout neural_guarded utility 0.3564 vs baseline -1.4642, reach 12.50% vs 8.33%.
claims.title: Signal replay-certified WASD ranker improves held-out control utility

claims.claim_text: A guarded Signal neural_active live pilot executes checkpoint-ranked WASD actions on a running local server with logged active-source, checkpoint hash, inference latency, protocol compatibility, safety gates, damage/death telemetry, and replay-ready trace rows.

supported_if: protocol_checked_rows >= 50 and protocol_compatible_rows >= 50 from runtime PROTOCOL_INFO frames

claims.limitation_when_not_supported: The live Signal pilot is not supported as neural-active by the current live-brain artifact, so only offline replay and shadow evidence should be reported.

It does not yet show that active neural control improves utility or safety versus the heuristic baseline.
claims.summary: the live Signal pilot did run checkpoint-ranked neural actions, but only behind guards: 74 recent neural-source rows from checkpoint f12b644ed9fa, p95 inference 0.089 ms, 74 replay-ready rows, protocol-compatible rows=74, safety-gate rows=74, damage events=2, deaths=0; no baseline comparison is claimed.
claims.title: Signal guarded neural-active pilot executes live checkpoint-ranked actions
